LESSON: DANGERS OF HEAT

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Environment 1.6 Energy: Heat By the end of the sub-strand, the  Using relevant 
Topic 1.6.3: Dangers of heat

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Dangers of heat. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which materials b) identify dangers of heat energy at  Learners are guided to identify cause fire?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat
4. tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: DANGERS OF HEAT
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 3
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Dangers of heat helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: DANGERS OF HEAT
Dangers of heat is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangers of heat” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Dangers of heat matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dangers of heat this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangers of heat” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Dangers of heat is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangers of heat” around your school. (skill: explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Dangers of heat matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Dangers of heat this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Dangers of heat” around your school. (skill: tell why Dangers of heat matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Dangers of heat to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Dangers of heat.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Dangers of heat from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Dangers of heat: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 3 learner study Dangers of heat?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which materials b) identify dangers of heat energy at  Learners are guided to identify cause fire?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Dangers of heat means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Dangers of heat means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Dangers of heat appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
